answer:
## Hypothesis (direct answer)

**In the pooled 100-year-bin PCA of the 12 capital Z-variables (4300–500 BCE, PC1 = 31.8% of variance; sign fixed once so the Copper&Gold loading ZCU_AU is positive), PC1 at 1100 BCE is +4.45 — a sharp positive outlier that is the maximum of the entire 39-bin series — while all subsequent Younger Bronze Age horizons drop to a band of +0.82 to +2.17 (mean +1.44). The 1100 BCE value exceeds the 1000–500 BCE mean by +3.01 units (1.61 SD of the full series; 5.8 SD within the YBA horizons) and exceeds even the nearest successor (1000 BCE) by +2.28 units (1.22 SD). Because PC1 loads positively on symbolic (Hatchets&Swords +0.30, Daggers +0.28, House Size +0.23), social (Copper&Gold +0.40, Monument Count +0.19) and economic (Depot +0.34, Monument Size +0.24) accumulation markers — with Amber (−0.26), Axes&Celts (−0.26) and Pottery Form (−0.36) on the opposite pole — PC1 can be read as an "integral capital-accumulation" axis. On that axis, 1100 BCE is the hypothesis' key anomaly: symbolic, social and economic capital spike simultaneously at the very beginning of the Younger Bronze Age and then collapse. Decomposing the 1100-vs-later gap by variable confirms the drivers are Copper&Gold (+1.15), Depot (+0.80), House Size (+0.47), Dagger (+0.44) and Monument Count (+0.36) — social capital contributes most (≈+1.5 of the +3.0 gap), then symbolic (≈+0.9) and economic (≈+0.9), while pottery/pottery-decoration trends slightly against it. The shape after the spike is a step-down followed by partial, non-monotonic recovery — 1000: +2.17 → 900: +1.65 → an 800 BCE rebound to +1.91 → 700: +1.25 → 600: +0.83 → 500: +0.82 — i.e., not a flat new level but a decaying trend toward zero that plateaus at ~+0.8 by 600–500 BCE, with the 800 BCE rebound (roughly coinciding with the onset of strongly rising Belau pollen openness, though that record ends at 702 BCE and cannot cover 700–500 BCE) preventing a strictly monotonic reading. Context: elevated PC1 (+3.3 to +3.8) already occurs at 1400–1200 BCE, so 1100 BCE caps a Late Bronze Age high-accumulation phase; the genuinely YBA-specific signal is the abrupt discontinuity after 1100 BCE — the society never returns to that PC1 level anywhere in the following 600 years.**

## Supporting tables (primary run: mean-centered SVD on the supplied z-values; sign convention as stated)

PC1 scores, YBA window (sensitivity run with column re-standardization in brackets):
| BCE | 1100 | 1000 | 900 | 800 | 700 | 600 | 500 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PC1 | **+4.452** [+4.506] | +2.172 [+2.176] | +1.654 [+1.649] | +1.910 [+1.919] | +1.247 [+1.241] | +0.829 [+0.810] | +0.815 [+0.789] |

- PC1 variance explained: 31.8% (sensitivity 30.3%); PC2 20.4%, PC3 13.6%.
- Gap vs mean(1000–500)=+1.438: **+3.014 = 1.61 SD(all 39 bins, SD 1.87) = 5.83 SD(YBA 6-bin SD)**; gap vs max later (1000 BCE): +2.280 = 1.22 SD.
- Whole-series context: 1100 BCE ranks 39/39 (series max +4.45; series min −2.01 @ 3800 BCE); neighbors 1400/1300/1200 BCE = +3.84/+3.48/+3.31 — the spike caps a late-LBA high phase, followed by a permanent step-down.

PC1 loadings by capital form (fixed sign):
| form | loadings |
|---|---|
| symbolic | Hatchets&Swords +0.30, Daggers +0.28, House Size +0.23 |
| social | Copper&Gold **+0.40**, Amber −0.26, Monument Count +0.19 |
| cultural | Pottery Form −0.36, Pottery Decoration +0.38 |
| economic | Depot **+0.34**, Axes&Celts −0.26, Monument Size +0.24, Sickle −0.06 |

Gap decomposition (loading × (x₁₁₀₀ − mean x₁₀₀₀₋₅₀₀)), sum = +3.014: ZCU_AU +1.145, ZHort +0.797, Zhausgr +0.466, ZDolch +0.441, ZMonument +0.358, all others |·|≤0.21 → by form: social +1.47, symbolic +0.91, economic +0.85, cultural −0.21. This confirms the researcher-flagged driver set (Copper&Gold, Depot, Dagger, House Size, Monument Count spiking at 1100 and collapsing by 1000) from the loadings, not by assumption.

## Methods, assumptions, sensitivity (kept visible)
- Authoritative input: capital.csv, 39 unique 100-year bins 4300–500 BCE, zero missing values, 12 Z columns (file spells `ZSichel`); annual `*_inter` columns excluded; rows already in 100-year bins (no rebinning).
- Single pooled PCA over all 39 bins chosen because a PCA within the 7-bin YBA slice is rank-degenerate (ZSichel & ZKeform constant; SVD fails after within-slice standardization). "Beginning" = the single 1100 BCE bin.
- Headline numbers from the primary (mean-centered only) run; the re-standardized sensitivity run reproduces every YBA score to ≤0.06 and every conclusion (gap 1.61 SD both runs).
- PC1 sign is arbitrary; all interpretation is carried by loadings and gaps (sign-invariant when stated together).
- Pollen/Belau_PC1 excluded from the PCA; used only as one-sentence context, and its record terminates at 702 BCE — the 700–500 BCE "coincidence" cannot be evaluated from it.
- Limitation: PC1 mixes capital forms with mixed-sign loadings (potteryDecoration vs potteryForm on opposite poles), so it is a general intensification axis, not a pure "total capital" measure; conclusions about the magnitude/sign of the 1100 anomaly are robust, the fine shape (800 BCE rebound = +0.26 above 900) is within the noise expected from n=1 bins.

Executed, nonempty script: `analysis_pca_capital.py` (full console log in `analysis_output.txt`).

payload.hypothesis: In the pooled 100-year-bin PCA of the 12 capital Z-variables (PC1 = 31.8% of variance; sign fixed so the Copper&Gold loading is positive), PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.45) is the maximum of the entire 4300-500 BCE series and stands 3.01 units (1.61 whole-series SD; 5.8 within-YBA SD) above the mean of the 1000-500 BCE horizons, which occupy only +0.82 to +2.17. PC1 loads positively on symbolic (Hatchets&Swords +0.30, Daggers +0.28, House Size +0.23), social (Copper&Gold +0.40, Monument Count +0.19) and economic (Depot +0.34, Monument Size +0.24) accumulation markers, so 1100 BCE represents a simultaneous one-bin spike of social, symbolic and economic capital — gap decomposition: Copper&Gold +1.15, Depot +0.80, House Size +0.47, Dagger +0.44, Monument Count +0.36 — that collapses by 1000 BCE and is followed by a partial, non-monotonic recovery (dip at 900, rebound at 800, plateau ~+0.8 by 600-500 BCE) that never approaches the 1100 BCE level; the anomaly caps a Late Bronze Age high-accumulation phase (1400-1200 BCE also elevated) and marks a permanent post-1100 BCE step-down in overall capital intensity.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (decimal=',') -> verified 39 unique 100-year bins 4300-500 BCE, zero missing, 12 Z columns; PCA = mean-centered SVD on all 39 bins x 12 columns (primary), with a column-re-standardized sensitivity run; fixed PC1 sign so ZCU_AU loading > 0; extracted PC1 scores for 1100 and 1000-500 BCE, computed gaps in raw and SD units, whole-series rank of 1100 BCE, loadings grouped by the four capital forms, and a per-variable decomposition of the 1100-vs-1000-500 gap; pollen files inspected and used only as one flagged context sentence (record ends 702 BCE). Script: analysis_pca_capital.py; output log: analysis_output.txt.
